pages.text: Take one mouth of a wormhole on a fast round trip: it ages less (twin paradox). Once its time lag exceeds the light-travel time between the mouths, the pair is a time machine - a closed timelike curve. Near that threshold, vacuum fluctuations pile up (Hawking's chronology protection).
$(thing)Set$(): Mouth speed, Trip duration, Mouth separation, Steering field.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): Mouth trajectory error: the trip speed is v·(1 ± 0.01%·d).

$(thing)Limits$(): No closed timelike curve yet: the lag is shorter than the light time; Chronology protection: vacuum polarisation diverges at the Cauchy horizon; Close to the chronology horizon: the structure strains; Steering field too weak for that turnaround; Interlock: mouth-steering coils not superconducting (too warm); Field above the critical field: the mouth-steering coils quench.$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): Loops run at a fixed pace.

$(thing)Equations$()$(br)Lorentz factor: γ = 1/√(1 − v²)$(br)Time lag: Δt = T(1 − 1/γ)$(br)Light time: t_L = L/c$(br)Loop length: Δt − L/c$(br)Lag / light time: Δt/(L/c)$(br)Turnaround acceleration: a = γvc/(T/2)$(br)Critical field: B_c(T) = B_c2(0)·(1 − (T/T_c)²)
